source_wording: Zoomed out, the division is one symbol and is drawn up the railway, the short way. Its two brigades went round by Novaliches (S65 pp. 186-188): zoom in to see them.
notes: Through Tinajeros, Malinta.

source_wording: S65 p. 188: "it was necessary to repair the railway over which the advance had been made"
notes: Through Meycauayan, Marilao, Bocaue, Bigaa, Guiguinto.

source_wording: The reports give the two places. The advance was up the Manila-Dagupan railway, and the route is drawn along it through the stations between.
notes: Straight from one to the other.

source_wording: S65 p. 194: "MacArthur's success at Santo Tomas and San Fernando"
notes: Through Apalit, Santo Tomas (Pampanga).

source_wording: S80 p. 152: began his advance on the 5th; three days to Mabalacat.
notes: Up the railway.

source_wording: S74: "MacArthur's troops occupied Capas yesterday"; Bell entered Tarlac the next evening.
notes: Through Capas.

source_wording: The reports give the two places. The advance was up the Manila-Dagupan railway, and the route is drawn along it through the stations between.
notes: Through Paniqui, Moncada.

source_wording: S65 p. 189: "With these troops in several cascoes, towed by three of our gunboats, he proceeded across the lake on April 9"
notes: Straight from one to the other. Drawn clear of the land; the track is not in the report.

source_wording: S65 p. 190: "He returned on April 17". The way back is taken to be the way out.
notes: Through Manila.

source_wording: S65 p. 191: Lawton "started from near Caloocan on April 22" by Novaliches and San Jose; "He in person reached Nozagaray on April 25"
notes: Through Novaliches, San Jose del Monte.

source_wording: The reports give the two places, not the road. Drawn along the main road through the towns between.
notes: Through Angat, San Rafael.

source_wording: S65 p. 196: "The enemy has a large force at San Ildefonso and San Miguel"; Lawton took both on 14-15 May.
notes: Through San Ildefonso.

source_wording: S65 p. 201: "Lawton descending the Rio Grande"
notes: Through Cabiao.

source_wording: The reports give the two places, not the road. Drawn along the main road through the towns between.
notes: Through Mexico.

source_wording: S74: troops crossed "to the east bank of the river" at Arayat for "an advance on Cabiao".
notes: Straight from one to the other.

source_wording: The reports give the two places, not the road. Drawn along the main road through the towns between.
notes: Through Santa Rosa.

source_wording: S68 gives this road for Young (San Jose, Lupao, Humingan); that Lawton followed it is taken from his being behind Young.
notes: Through San Jose (Nueva Ecija), Lupao, Umingan.

source_wording: S74: Lawton's telegram of 17 Nov is dated "on road between San Nicolas and San Manuel".
notes: Through San Manuel, Binalonan.

source_wording: The reports give the two places, not the road. Drawn along the main road through the towns between.
notes: Through Binalonan.

source_wording: S80 p. 144: Young "took the wagon road from Santa Ana" for Arayat.
notes: Through Mexico and Santa Ana.

source_wording: S68: Young's road by San Jose; S80 p. 148: San Jose on the 12th.
notes: Through Talavera.

source_wording: S80 p. 154: Young set out from Pozorrubio on the 17th.
notes: Through Binalonan, where Batson was on the 16th (S75).

source_wording: S75 (Batson): "marched my battalion through Alava to San Rosario". Alava is today's Sison.
notes: Through Sison (Alava).

source_wording: S75 (Batson): "I arrived at Tubao about 12 o'clock noon", then the ford of the Aringay River.
notes: Through Tubao.

source_wording: The coast road; S68 has Aguinaldo a day ahead "on the coast road".
notes: Through Caba, Bauang.

source_wording: The coast road. S68: "Swigert examined country around Namacpacan, Balauang, and Bangar."
notes: Through San Juan (La Union), Bacnotan, Balaoan.

source_wording: The coast road north; S68 has Tinio holding trenches across it at Tagudin.
notes: Through Bangar, Tagudin, Santa Cruz (Ilocos Sur), Santa Lucia, Candon, Santiago (Ilocos Sur), Santa Maria (Ilocos Sur).

source_wording: The reports give the two places, not the road. Drawn along the main road through the towns between.
notes: Through Santa.

source_wording: S65 p. 198: up the Rio Grande with the gunboats; they had "a sharp engagement at San Luis".
notes: Through San Luis (Pampanga).

source_wording: S74: "He sailed on the morning of November 6, and arrived opposite San Fabian the following day." The track is not given: drawn out past Corregidor, up the Zambales coast and round Cape Bolinao.
notes: Straight from one to the other. Drawn clear of the land; the track is not in the report.

source_wording: S74: "He sailed on the morning of November 6, and arrived opposite San Fabian the following day." The track is not given: drawn out past Corregidor, up the Zambales coast and round Cape Bolinao, then from the ships to the beach.
notes: Straight from one to the other. Drawn clear of the land; the track is not in the report.

source_wording: S68 gives Candon and the pass; the trail between is drawn through the towns at the foot of it.
notes: Through Salcedo, Concepcion (Gregorio del Pilar).

source_wording: S71 marks the fight of 2 Dec "between Lingay and Angaqui"; March reached Cervantes on the 3rd.
notes: Through Angaqui.

source_wording: S74 (Batchelor): "I expect to reach Ilagan in about five days and Aparri on or about December 12." Down the Cagayan valley; the towns between are those on the valley road today.
notes: Through Solano, Bagabag, Cordon, Santiago (Isabela), Cauayan, Ilagan, Tumauini, Cabagan, Tuguegarao, Iguig, Amulung.

source_wording: S68, printing Lawton's letter of 19 Nov: Aguinaldo "passed out via Urdaneta, Manaoag and Pozorubio".
notes: Through Urdaneta and Manaoag (S68). S80 has him go by train some twenty miles north, then twelve miles east across country; it names no stations (C-LZ11).

source_wording: S80 p. 148: "on the fifteenth Aguinaldo turned north and west, crossing the mountains into La Union".
notes: Over the mountains into La Union (S80). The trail is not given: drawn through Rosario and Tubao, where Young followed it (S75).

source_wording: S68: "Aguinaldo slept in Balauang, on the coast road".
notes: Through Bauang, San Fernando (La Union), San Juan, Bacnotan.

source_wording: S68: he "passed through Bangar 10 a. m. November 21"; on up the coast road to Candon.
notes: Through Bangar, Tagudin, Santa Cruz (Ilocos Sur), Santa Lucia.

source_wording: S68: "by mountain trail southeast to Lepanto", "leaving Pilar to fortify and hold the mountain pass in his rear, near Angaqui".
notes: Through Salcedo, Concepcion (Gregorio del Pilar), Tirad Pass.

source_wording: S65 p. 188: MacArthur "pressed northward the enemy who stubbornly contested every village"; it retreated from Malolos on Calumpit.
notes: Through Meycauayan, Marilao, Bocaue, Bigaa, Guiguinto, Malolos.

source_wording: Driven from Santo Tomas and San Fernando on 4-5 May, in MacArthur's front until the 17th (S65 pp. 194, 197, 200). The symbol moves up the railway through those days.
notes: Through Apalit, Santo Tomas (Pampanga), San Fernando (Pampanga).

source_wording: S65 p. 200: "Luna had retreated on Tarlac". Drawn up the railway.
notes: Through Mabalacat, Bamban, Capas.

source_wording: S65 p. 196: "a large force at San Ildefonso and San Miguel".
notes: Through San Ildefonso.

source_wording: The coast road north, ahead of Young.
notes: His way to Vigan is not given: drawn up the coast road ahead of Young. S80 has the attackers come down the Abra River by boat.

source_wording: S65 pp. 186-188: Otis's brigade, "keeping to the left and retired", was to strike the Novaliches road near Balintauag.
notes: Straight from one to the other.

source_wording: S65 pp. 186-188: "Hale's brigade to that point by San Francisco del Monte and Bagbag"
notes: Through San Francisco del Monte.

source_wording: S65 pp. 186-188: "both brigades marched towards the railway" by "the road which strikes the railway south of Polo".
notes: Straight from one to the other.

source_wording: S65 pp. 186-188: "both brigades marched towards the railway" by "the road which strikes the railway south of Polo".
notes: Straight from one to the other.
Straight from one to the other.
Straight from one to the other.

source_wording: S65 p. 189: "towed by three of our gunboats, he proceeded across the lake on April 9". The track is not given: drawn down the Pasig and round the south of Talim Island, as the expedition's is.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S65 p. 190: "He returned on April 17". The way back is taken to be the way out.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S65 p. 195: "from Manila to Guagua"; "He found the entrance of the Guagua River without difficulty, proceeded up stream until Sexmoan was reached". Drawn across the head of Manila Bay; the channel is not given.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S65 p. 196: back to Manila, then "to find the mouth of the Rio Grande and pass up that stream to Calumpit". The call at Manila on the 9th is not drawn.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S65 p. 198: up the Rio Grande by San Luis to Candaba.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S65 p. 200: "Kobbe and gunboats started up river this morning at six."
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S75 (Parker): up the coast to the anchorage near Vigan. Drawn clear of the land.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S74 (Young): "I left Vigan 8 a. m. on Samar, reaching Laoag" that afternoon. Drawn clear of the land.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S75 (Parker): "The Oregon has gone to Vigan." Drawn clear of the land.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S74: she reached San Fabian on the 27th with news of Vigan. Drawn clear of the land.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S74: "one company proceeding to that point by gunboat which would reach there the following day". Drawn clear of the land.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S74: by the gunboat Callao to Vigan, then ashore. Drawn clear of the land.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S74 (Young): "I left Vigan 8 a. m. on Samar, reaching Laoag" that afternoon. Drawn clear of the land, then ashore.
notes: By water. The track is not in the report.

source_wording: S65 p. 163: "At 11:20 a. m. Stotsenburg is crossing San Juan River at the bridge"; then "captured the powder house and Deposito".
notes: The road from the San Juan bridge to the reservoir as the engineer map (S78) draws it. That the regiment kept to the road is an inference.

source_wording: S65 p. 163: "The Nebraska regiment and Tennessee battalion advanced rapidly during the morning and captured the powder house and Deposito"
notes: By the Santa Mesa road and the San Juan bridge, as the engineer map (S78) draws them. The battalion's own route is not stated.

source_wording: S65 p. 165 (Anderson, 12:30): "Last seen of Smith (Colonel of California regiment meaning) was advancing on the right with two battalions and entering San Pedro Macati."
notes: "On the right" is all the report says of the way: drawn clear of Santa Ana to the south, from the right of King's line to the town. Not along any road read from a map. Re-placed 21 Nov 2026 with the rows it joins.

source_wording: S80 p. 144: he crossed the Rio Grande on the 17th and moved up the east bank toward Cabiao.
notes: Straight from one to the other.

source_wording: S80 p. 148: from San Jose to Umingan; S68 gives Lupao on the road.
notes: Through Lupao.

source_wording: S80 p. 148: from Umingan the cavalry went on to Tayug and San Nicolas.
notes: Straight from one to the other.

source_wording: S80 p. 152: on to Bamban, up the railway.
notes: Up the railway.

source_wording: S80 p. 153: reconnoitered to the railway's terminus at Dagupan.
notes: Drawn by Calasiao, near the railway; the line itself is not traced.

source_wording: S80 p. 155: arrived at San Fernando from San Fabian on the 25th.
notes: By the coast road through Aringay, Caba and Bauang; the day it left is not stated.

source_wording: S80 p. 155: at Namacpacan on the 26th.
notes: By the coast road.

source_wording: S80 p. 155: sent "toward Candon to block Tirad Pass".
notes: By the coast road.

source_wording: S80 p. 155: after San Jacinto Tinio "had pieced together" 600 men outside Namacpacan.
notes: His way north is not given: drawn up the coast road.

source_wording: S80 p. 157: Hare hiked up the east coast of Lingayen Gulf, garrisoning the main towns of La Union and Ilocos Sur.
notes: By the coast road; the day he left San Fabian is not stated.

source_wording: S80 p. 157: "Marching twenty miles in one day".
notes: By the coast road.

source_wording: S80 p. 151: the 36th joined Fowler at Mangatarem on the 26th.
notes: Its way is not given: straight.
